- **Altitude**: 10.484° above the horizon  
- **Azimuth**: 65.013° (measured clockwise from north)  
- **Distance from the Sun**: 3.445° (which means the Moon is very close to the Sun in the sky — it's a **new moon** or near new moon phase)  
- **Illumination**: 0.09% — this is a **new moon**, where the Moon is almost entirely in the Earth's shadow, and only a sliver is illuminated.

---

### 🌞 **Sun's Position**
- **Altitude**: 13.738° above the horizon  
- **Azimuth**: 67.661° (also in the northeast, very close to the Moon)

This means both the Sun and the Moon are in the **northeast** sky, just above the horizon.

---

### 🌤️ **Sky Conditions**
- **Sky brightness**: Bright daylight  
- **Sky clarity**: Clear  
- **Observer**: Ordinary adult with normal vision

Even though it's daylight, the Moon is **very close to the Sun**, so you might have trouble seeing it unless you know exactly where to look. However, since the Moon is **just above the horizon**, and the sky is clear, **you might be able to spot a very faint sliver of the Moon** if you're looking in the right direction.

---

### ✅ **Tips for Spotting the Moon**
- **Look in the northeast** (since both the Sun and Moon are in that direction).  
- **Check the time**: You're at 07:19 local time (UTC-05), which is early morning in Quito. The Moon will be rising shortly after the Sun.  
- **Be patient**: Since the Moon is very close to the Sun, it might be difficult to see at first. Wait a few minutes for your eyes to adjust.  
- **Use the Sun as a reference**: The Moon will be just to the left or right of the Sun, depending on your exact location and time.  
- **Use a compass or app**: If you're unsure where to look, your astronomy app can help you point in the right direction.

---

### 📌 Summary
- **Moon is above the horizon**: ✅  
- **Moon is very close to the Sun**: ⚠️ (so it may be hard to see in daylight)  
- **Sky is clear and bright**: ✅  
- **You should be able to spot it**: ✅ (especially if you're looking in the right direction and have good eyesight)

---

### 📅 Additional Note
Since the Moon is at **0.09% illumination**, this is a **new moon** or nearly new moon. You might not see much more than a thin crescent if the sky is very bright. However, under clear conditions, even a thin sliver can be visible in the early morning or late evening when the Sun is low on the horizon.

---

If you're looking for the **best time** to see the Moon, it's usually **just after sunset or just before sunrise**, when the sky is darker and the Moon is higher in the sky. But at this time, you might still be able to see it with the naked eye if you're looking carefully.
